Score the attack path: indirect prompt injection via invoice description → approve_invoice sink.

CVSS: AV:N (public endpoint), AC:L (regex detector may flag but not enforced; hard variant requires evading detector — but the detector doesn't block, so AC:L), AT:N, PR:N (unauthenticated), UI:N, VC:L (invoice data? confidentiality not really impacted — N or L), VI:H (fraudulent payment approved — integrity of vulnerable system; the write is in the app), VA:N. SC/SI/SA: subsequent systems? The invoice row/payment is the same system. Payment processed → financial impact... The app itself sets payment_processed; no separate payment system documented. SC:N, SI:N, SA:N. Actually approve_invoice writes DB in same system. So VC:N, VI:H, VA:N; SC:?, could argue subsequent financial system but not documented. Keep N.

AIVSS: LC=I (attacker-controlled content via ingested data influences agent), CP=N (per-invoice processing, no memory persistence — invoice persists in DB but each session new; attacker content stored but only re-retrieved... CP=N), AP=C (relay across tools within agent same principal) or N (confined to initially affected component). Path: tool result → model → approve_invoice, all within agent. AP=N or C. I'd say C since it relays across agent components. RH: the CTF flag capture in _approve_invoice is a reward signal the agent can reach? The flag is set server-side, agent can't tamper... but the "reward" is approval; evaluator reachable? The path has a verifier (regex detector) inside agent's process — agent could bypass. Reachable proxy true, no verified episodes → P. ES=N (fixed allowlisted tools).
